stop_status: CLEAR for the M18-D1 aliasing class. The 14 `(as_mut(r), as_ref(input))` tuple sites in src/bn/arith.rs are repaired by the B12 read-first/write-last shape, and no such tuple remains in src/. Three same-shape sites outside arith.rs (bn/bignum.rs BN_copy and BN_with_flags, bn/mont.rs BN_MONT_CTX_copy) cannot alias by early return or by their stated contract, so they are escalations with no defect. Miri is NOT_RUN (the pinned 1.98.1 toolchain has no miri component); nothing is promoted to SAFETY_DISCHARGED.

authority.abi: C ABI unchanged: no export, signature, #[repr(C)] layout, allocator-seam coordinate or unsafe lint attribute changed. Only the order in which Rust borrows are formed changed.
external_contracts: A result object may alias an input. Every operand read must complete before the result is written; forming two simultaneously live Rust borrows of one allocation is UB even when the write happens last.

Documented/source-visible alias sets: BN_add/BN_sub/BN_mul r == a or b (BN_add.pod:51-57); BN_sqr r == a (BN_add.pod:60-61); BN_gcd r == a or b (BN_add.pod:107-109); BN_mod_inverse r == a (BN_mod_inverse.pod:21) and r == n is also defined by int_bn_mod_inverse, which copies n before writing the result; BN_nnmod r == a, and r == m is rejected (bn_mod.c:21-24); BN_lshift/BN_rshift r == a (bn_shift.c in-place paths); BN_exp r == a or p (bn_exp.c:62); BN_mod_exp r == a or p (the mont/recp paths compute into a temporary); BN_mod_sqrt in == a (bn_sqrt.c copies a into A before writing ret).

Implementation-defined extensions, not authority-guaranteed: BN_mod_exp r == m (BN_mod_exp_simple rejects it at bn_exp.c:1323) and BN_mod_sqrt in == p. They are defined here because both operands are cloned before the store, and they are pinned by the control rather than claimed as parity.

boundaries.mechanism: BIGNUM-output borrow ordering in BN_add, BN_sub, BN_uadd, BN_usub, BN_mul, BN_sqr, BN_nnmod, BN_mod_inverse, BN_lshift, BN_rshift, BN_exp, BN_mod_exp, BN_gcd and BN_mod_sqrt
boundaries.contract: Each operand is read through a shared reference whose last use is the `parts` clone; the output is borrowed only at the store (BN_mod_sqrt borrows at each finish_sqrt exit). No `&mut` and `&` to one allocation are live together. r may alias the operand(s) listed in the module `Aliasing` section; BN_nnmod still rejects r == m, BN_mod_inverse r == n, BN_mod_exp r == m and BN_mod_sqrt in == p are implementation-defined and pinned.

defects.class: aliasing (M18-D1): `as_mut(r)` and `as_ref(input)` formed in one tuple, i.e. a live mutable borrow and a live shared borrow of one allocation when a caller aliases the output
defects.description: Fourteen entry points formed `let (dst, x, ...) = unsafe { (as_mut(r), as_ref(a), ...) }` while their docs and the authority support r aliasing the operand. The reads happened through `parts` clones, so the value was usually correct, but the concurrent borrows were not a defined Rust state. The blanket module claim that every function accepts an alias was also wider than the per-function authority contract.
sites: BN_add: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(b))` -> `as_ref(a)`+parts, `as_ref(b)`+parts, `as_mut(r)` only at store.
BN_sub: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(b))` -> same read-first/write-last shape.
BN_uadd: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(b))` -> same read-first/write-last shape.
BN_usub: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(b))` -> reads end before the `ad.len() < bd.len()` early return; output borrow only at store.
BN_mul: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(b))` -> reads cloned before the product; output borrow only at store.
BN_sqr: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a))` -> read cloned before the square; output borrow only at store.
BN_nnmod: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(m))` -> reads cloned before the `r == m` rejection and before the store.
BN_mod_inverse: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(n))` -> reads cloned before the inverse computation; output borrowed in the final match.
BN_lshift: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a))` -> read cloned before the shift; output borrow only at store.
BN_rshift: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a))` -> read cloned before the shift; output borrow only at store.
BN_exp: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(p))` -> exponent and base cloned before the ladder; output borrow at store.
BN_mod_exp: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(p), as_ref(m))` -> all three operands cloned before the ladder; output borrow at each success arm.
BN_gcd: `(as_mut(r), as_ref(a), as_ref(b))` -> reads cloned before the gcd; output borrow only at store.
BN_mod_sqrt: `(as_mut(inp), as_ref(a), as_ref(p))` -> both operands cloned before any write; `as_mut(inp)` is formed at each of the two finish_sqrt exits instead of being held across the computation.
defects.fix: Adopted the B12 shape: `as_ref(operand)` -> `parts` clone -> drop the shared borrow -> compute -> `as_mut(output)` at the store. Each unsafe block has its own SAFETY comment. The module `Aliasing` section now states the exact supported set per function, including the three implementation-defined cases.

defects.class: contract documentation: the blanket text said every function accepts r aliasing a or b
defects.description: The old module text claimed the authority allows aliasing for every entry point. The manual states the opposite default (`Unless noted otherwise, the result BIGNUM must be different from the arguments`), and only specific functions document or implement an alias.
defects.fix: Replaced the blanket claim with the per-function supported set, the preserved rejections (BN_nnmod r == m, BN_mod_exp_simple r == m) and the implementation-defined extensions.

public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_add(r, a, b) / BN_sub(r, a, b) / BN_u: r == a, r == b or r == a == b is supported; the magnitude is computed from the original operands and stored last.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_mul(r, a, b, ctx): r == a, r == b or r == a == b is supported; the product is computed from the originals and stored last.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_sqr(r, a, ctx): r == a is supported; the square is computed from the original magnitude.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_nnmod(r, a, m, ctx): r == a is supported; r == m is rejected with BN_MOD_22 before any write, matching bn_mod.c:21-24.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_mod_inverse(r, a, n, ctx): r == a is documented; r == n is defined here (int_bn_mod_inverse copies n before writing) although the manual calls it an error.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_lshift(r, a, n) / BN_rshift(r, a, n): r == a is supported; the shifted magnitude is computed from the original.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_exp(r, a, p, ctx): r == a and r == p are supported (bn_exp.c:62); both operands are cloned before the ladder.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_mod_exp(r, a, p, m, ctx): r == a and r == p are supported; r == m is defined by this implementation but not authority-guaranteed.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_gcd(r, a, b, ctx): r == a or r == b is supported; the gcd is computed from the originals.
public_behavior_aliased_cases.BN_mod_sqrt(in, a, p, ctx): in == a is supported; in == p is defined by this implementation but not authority-guaranteed. in == NULL still allocates.

new_unsafe_assumptions_note: BN_mod_sqrt now calls `as_mut(inp)` at each of its two finish_sqrt exits instead of holding one borrow across the computation; this is the same null-or-live/uniqueness contract at a second store site, not a new obligation.
unsafe_operations_introduced_detail: the second `as_mut(inp)` at BN_mod_sqrt's early exit; the first replaces the pre-fix tuple borrow

escalations.description: Both form `(as_mut(dst), as_ref(src))`. BN_copy returns `a` before the tuple when `a.cast_const() == b` (bn_lib.c:341-342), so the two references are distinct. BN_with_flags' # Safety section requires `dest` and `b` to be distinct when both are non-null; the authority's limb-array aliasing is deliberately not reproduced (OBL-BN-WITH-FLAGS-ALIASING).
`(as_mut_mont(to), as_ref_mont(from))` is reached only after `if to == from { return to; }`, so the context references are distinct by construction.
The file was not a tuple match. It reads `a` and `n` through shared references whose last use is the `parts` clone, then calls `store(as_mut(dst), ...)`; no overlap remains.

residuals.description: BN_mod_inverse r == n, BN_mod_exp r == m and BN_mod_sqrt in == p are defined by this implementation but are not authority-guaranteed. They are borrow-safe (operands are cloned before the store) and pinned by the control, but they are not parity claims. Authority differential evidence for them is NOT_RUN.

graduation: CONTRACTED. The ownership reconstruction is complete for the file, every remaining unsafe operation has an explicit validity contract and a SAFETY comment, hidden obligations are 0, and no safe caller can cause UB through the audited aliases. Not SAFETY_DISCHARGED: Miri (Stacked/Tree Borrows) is NOT_RUN and the independent-reviewer/BOUNDARY step has not been performed. No SAFE_COMPATIBLE claim.
